newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil spending to rise on short term - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil spending to rise on short term - report.

text.p: Measures to tackle Brazil's public deficit, such as voluntary redundancy programs, will in the short-term increase federal spending, a Central Bank director told a newspaper.

Francisco Lopes, Director of Monetary Policy, said in an interview published in Wednesday's Jornal do Brasil that Brazil's fiscal performance in 1997 would be "substantially better" than 1996's "mediocre" result.
"Our preoccupation with the fiscal area is permanent," the newspaper quoted Lopes as saying. "In Brazil we must create a primary surplus...of 1.5 percent of gross domestic product."

Lopes said Brasilia had learned two lessons: it was hard to correct the errors of the past and in the short-term there could be a conflict between reform of the state and the deficit. "For example, voluntary redundancy programs increase short-term expenditure but the gains are long-term. Transitorially, then, we are raising expenditure," he said.
Lopes said the outlook for 1997 was "very good," with projected single-digit inflation and average GDP growth above 4.0 percent a year and better fiscal figures.
"We will have a substantial improvement in the federal area, raising revenue and cutting costs," he said.
"In 1997, we will have a different picture to 1996, when the fiscal performance was mediocre," he added.

Lopes also said the government would not allow the economy to overheat. But he said stabilization had taken such a hold on the economy that macroeconomic management could be achieved with "fine adjustments."
"Now we can use classical measures and no longer credit controls," he said.
